turns.text: My tomato plants have pale leaves and the fruit is slow. What is going on?
Pale leaves on tomatoes usually mean feeding or light. Let us work through it.
They are in pots on a balcony that gets sun from midday.
Midday sun is enough. The usual gap is feed: tomatoes in pots need a weekly feed once fruit sets.
I have not fed them at all this year. Which feed should I use?
A tomato feed high in potash, once a week. Note your constraint: the balcony tap drips, so watering is by can.
Also the pots are small, 5 litre ones. Is that a problem?
Five litre pots dry out fast and limit roots. Ten litres or more is the comfortable size for a cordon tomato.
I cannot repot now, they are fruiting. What else can I do?
Then water little and often, feed weekly, and mulch the surface to hold moisture.
My neighbour said to strip all the side shoots. Should I?
Only for cordon types. If yours is a bush type, leave the shoots alone.
It says cordon on the label. Fine. What about the pale leaves coming back?
If pale leaves return after two weeks of feeding, check for magnesium deficiency: older leaves yellow between the veins.
And if it is magnesium?
An Epsom salt spray, one tablespoon per litre, once. Do not repeat it weekly.
Good. One more thing: the balcony is windy and the pots blow over.
Group the pots together against the wall and tie the canes to the railing.
Budget is tight this month, under 20 pounds for everything.
Feed and Epsom salts come to under 12 pounds at Fernhill, so the plan fits the budget.
Let me check: weekly potash feed, keep watering by can little and often, strip side shoots on the cordon, Epsom salts once only if the yellowing pattern matches.
That is the plan exactly. The pinned facts are: balcony tap drips so watering is by can; pots are 5 litre and cannot be repotted mid fruiting; the variety is a cordon; budget under 20 pounds.
And the feed must be high potash, weekly, once fruit has set. Thanks, that is everything.
You are welcome. If the leaves pale again in two weeks, bring a photo to the plant desk.
